transcript:
Header: 2025-09-18 14:00 PDT | Duration: 54m
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Jared Park (Redwood SE), Anita Rao (CloudX PM), Luis Martinez (CloudX Eng), Priya Singh (CloudX Security)

Summary:
Quick sync between Redwood and CloudX marketplace and integrations team to align on marketplace listing requirements, reference architecture options (hosted vs dedicated vs private), and validation plan for a joint listing + reference solution. High-level alignment on next steps and owners.

Topics: marketplace listing checklist, reference architecture (VPC/on-prem options), deployment templates (Terraform), performance validation, security/compliance (SOC2, KMS, RBAC), go-to-market notes.

Artifacts referenced: Draft listing doc: https://redwood.example/decks/cloudx-marketplace-draft Deck (pptx) link; Reference Arch folder: https://redwood.example/ra/cloudx ; Sample Terraform repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/cloudx-terraform (placeholder).

Transcript: 
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh we have about 50 minutes, so we'll run through the marketplace checklist, the RA options and then agree next steps, cool?
[00:12] Anita Rao: Yep this is Anita, thanks. Quick ask up front  CloudX has a marketplace approval checklist and then we need a reference architecture to go with the listing, right, typical.
[00:25] Jared Park: yeah exactly, we'll propose both a hosted listing workflow and then a dedicated and private (on-prem) variant. The RA will include VPC peering, SAML/SSO, and KMS notes.
[00:38] Luis Martinez: Quick context, our marketplace requires an install guide, sample deploy, and a verified perf run for the listing "verified" badge. Our customers care about latency esp 99th percentile and cost.
[00:52] Priya Singh: From security, we need to see SOC2 artifacts, audit logs retention, and an indication if the customer data ever leaves their VPC or Redwood's control plane. KMS (HSM) integration is a hard ask for some of our enterprise customers.
[01:10] Maya Chen: Understood. On the SOC2 and KMS side we have a public pack \u2014 we'll share SOC2 summary and KMS integration notes. For the RA we can show three deployment flavors: 1) Hosted (Redwood API listing, simple onboarding), 2) Dedicated (reserved GPU capacity in CloudX region or Redwood-managed) and 3) Private (customer-managed VPC or on-prem package).
[01:34] Anita Rao: ok that matches our expectations. For the marketplace listing we also need a short 1-page reference architecture diagram and Terraform examples for the customer to click-to-deploy, is that possible?
[01:46] Jared Park: Yes we can produce a simplified diagram for the listing and a more detailed RA in the RA folder. Terraform quick-starts are available \u2014 we'll tailor a small module that spins up the Dedicated config and the VPC connectors, timeline about a week.
[02:00] Anita Rao: timeline \u2014 we want listing live before Q4 push, so roughly end of September target. Doable?
[02:08] Maya Chen: That's tight but doable if we align this week on owners; we'll need sample workload for your perf team to validate.
[02:16] Luis Martinez: We'll provide an anonymized workload \u2014 sequences typically 64-512 tokens, 2k qps at peak for one of our reference customers, but that's probably more than your dedicated baseline, ok to scale down?
[02:28] Jared Park: Yeah we'll run a scaled validation; the important part is the distribution \u2014 the KV cache behavior and seq length distribution. Quick note \u2014 sometimes our transcripts call KV cache "K V cash" so apologies for typos, heh.
[02:40] Priya Singh: On encryption, we require that encryption keys stay in our KMS and that Redwood can use external KMS \u2014 is that supported?
[02:48] Maya Chen: Yes external KMS is supported in Private and Dedicated via customer-managed KMS; Hosted mode supports BYOK with certain limitations \u2014 we'll put the specifics in the KMS appendix.
[02:58] Anita Rao: Great. One compliance question \u2014 do you surface audit logs to the customer? Some marketplace reviews require evidence of audit trails.
[03:06] Jared Park: Yes logs are available \u2014 we can push audit logs into the customer's log sink (S3/Blob) or provide a log export. There are retention configs as well; we'll document the defaults and options.
[03:18] Anita Rao: Good. About the marketplace listing itself \u2014 what level of info do you need from us?
[03:25] Maya Chen: We need sample listing copy, logo, 1-line, features, supported regions, and a contact email; we'll draft and share and you can edit. Also we'll include a short reference arch one-pager.
[03:39] Luis Martinez: On the RA side, can you produce a variant that shows an air-gapped on-prem installation? A few of our customers need an air-gapped option.
[03:46] Jared Park: Yes we have an on-prem package that is typically a customer-managed deployment with a slimmed control plane and offline installers. We'll note caveats: updates and monitoring are different, and the E2E tests require a local runner.
[03:59] Anita Rao: Cool \u2014 any blockers we should be aware of?
[04:03] Maya Chen: Nothing technical blocker-wise; the main gating items are docs (the listing copy), a perf workload from your side, and a short security checklist confirmation. Once we have those we can run a validation and create the verification artifact for the marketplace.
[04:18] Priya Singh: For the security checklist, can you share your SOC2 summary and the data flow diagram so we can route it to our infosec?
[04:26] Maya Chen: Absolutely \u2014 I'll share the SOC2 summary and a high-level DFD in the RA folder.
[04:32] Anita Rao: Questions from our marketplace product team \u2014 what about pricing visibility for marketplace buyers? Do you expose unit pricing or is it negotiated?
[04:41] Maya Chen: We support either listing with a link to Redwood pricing; for many marketplace flows we provide a metered plan with per-token pricing and a link to an invoicing/contract flow. For Dedicated we have reserved capacity pricing which is contract-negotiated. We'll include the recommended pricing copy.
[04:58] Luis Martinez: Another engineering question \u2014 network topology for VPC peering vs Private link? Which do you recommend?
[05:06] Jared Park: For low-latency dedicated deployments, we typically recommend a PrivateLink style setup if the cloud provider supports it, otherwise VPC peering with proper routing. We'll add both topologies to the RA and call out latency tradeoffs.
[05:19] Anita Rao: Any PCI concerns if a partner wants to process payment data through the model?
[05:26] Priya Singh: Usually payments sensitive data shouldn't be sent to third-party inference without tokenization, so we'll flag that. Redwood, do you have guidance?
[05:34] Maya Chen: We recommend tokenization at the client side or using a private deployment where keys and data never leave the customer's VPC. We'll add a short security note to the listing.
[05:43] [crosstalk] Luis Martinez: okay \u2014 makes sense.
[05:46] Jared Park: Quick note on perf: we can provide a lightweight benchmark harness that runs your sample workload against a Redwood Dedicated config in one of our test clusters; results will include p50/p95/p99 and token throughput. It won't be production traffic but good enough for the verified badge.
[06:06] Anita Rao: That works. Who's owning the perf run?
[06:09] Maya Chen: Jared will lead the perf validation.
[06:12] Jared Park: Yep I'll schedule it once we get the workload.
[06:16] Priya Singh: On identity \u2014 marketplace requires SSO. We need SAML metadata to enable the marketplace-managed onboarding. Can you supply SP metadata and support SCIM?
[06:26] Maya Chen: We support SAML and SCIM. We'll share the SP metadata and a sample SCIM endpoint contract.
[06:33] Anita Rao: Great. A couple of notes on the listing flow: CloudX needs a short test that partners can pass to get the integrated badge. The test is basically deploy + perf validation + one security checklist signoff. That's our standard.
[06:46] Maya Chen: Good \u2014 that aligns with what we can deliver. We'll aim to have draft listing and RA ready for review by EOW.
[06:53] Luis Martinez: One more technical ask \u2014 are there any special kernel/quantization choices we recommend for medium latency workloads? Our customers often prefer quantized models to reduce infra costs.
[07:04] Jared Park: Yes, we'll include model & quantization recommendations per workload. For example 4-bit quantization on MPT-like models gives big cost wins but you should watch for slight quality regressions. We'll include rollback notes and recommended eval prompts.
[07:20] Anita Rao: Competitors are offering managed listings that hide pricing \u2014 our marketplace team wants clarity about unit economics. Please include a clear pricing blurb.
[07:29] Maya Chen: Will do.
[07:31] 
[07:31] Action recap: Maya to share SOC2 summary and draft listing; Jared to create RA diagrams + TF examples + run perf once we have workload; CloudX to send workload and compliance constraints.
[07:47] Anita Rao: Sounds good, thanks everyone. We'll plan to reconvene after the artifact drop, maybe a short follow-up next Tuesday.
[07:55] Maya Chen: Perfect \u2014 thanks all.

End of transcript.

Notes:
- Transcription shows normal conversational imperfections, occasional misheard acronyms (e.g., KV cache -> K V cash).
- Meeting ends with explicit next steps and action owners.
